rubrics.criterion: The precedence rules for the inherited presentation options are anchored in a single owner module in the changed tree: outside that one module, no module spells out its own precedence decision for these options, and modules that need a resolved value hand over their whole layer inputs (toast record + toaster-level values, stored record + update payload, per-toaster options + component props) or reuse the owner's documented answers.
rubrics.rationale: The task's central request is that the layering contract (which layer's value wins for duration, close button, invert, rich colors, built-in styling, icon, classNames carry-over, and the cancel/action button styles) is decided in exactly one place; this is the outcome a solver must reach, by whichever layout they choose.

rubrics.criterion: Every layer pair the scoped families actually exercise is served by that owner rather than left to per-site decisions: a toast record against toaster-level values at render time, per-toaster toastOptions against <Toaster> props during wiring, and an update payload against a stored record when a same-id toast is rebuilt.
rubrics.rationale: This instance scatters its copies across three kinds of layer pairs (render defaults, wiring-level layering, update carry-over); consolidating only the visible render sites while leaving the wiring or the store restating theirs would still leave a conceptual change touching several modules.

rubrics.criterion: The consumers were actually rewired to the consolidated owner: the toast render sites (expiry seeding and recomputation, close-button visibility, skin data attributes, icon selection, cancel/action button styles), the toaster-level wiring of the two layered options, and the store update path all route their values through the owner, and no former consumption site keeps a now-duplicated private decision alongside it.
rubrics.rationale: In this repository the precedence fragments sit at production consumption points; an owner that exists but is consulted by only some of them (the classic partially-adopted cleanup) leaves the very cross-module hunt the task complains about.

rubrics.criterion: A module that consumed a resolved value now bypasses the owner and re-derives the precedence it needs from raw layer inputs on its own, while the owner still exists for other sites.
rubrics.rationale: The realistic near-miss for this task is a regionally complete consolidation - the component, the wiring or the store keeps one private chain out of convenience - which a judge can verify directly against the patch without penalizing alternative owner layouts.

rubrics.criterion: Nothing that existed only to serve the old scattered arrangement is left dead behind the new one: the previous option-resolution helpers and modules that the consolidation replaced are removed (or repurposed with remaining callers), their dedicated type-only imports are dropped, and no per-site picker/splice helper left over from an abandoned approach still shadows a layer decision.
rubrics.rationale: Leaving superseded copies as apparently-live code (unused exports, an unimported module, stale precedence comments) is the natural residue of this specific cleanup in a package that spreads its modules flat under src/, and it is what a maintainer reviewing this PR would insist on.

rubrics.criterion: An artifact that only the old arrangement needed is still present and unreferenced: an entire module or an exported option-resolution helper remains in the tree although nothing inside the source imports it anymore.
rubrics.rationale: This is a concrete, checkable failure mode of the cleanup phase (grep-level evidence exists in the patch and the tree), distinct from the semantic outcomes; graders can confirm it from the patch and the checker output without any knowledge of a preferred final layout.

rubrics.criterion: The observable contract of the library is functionally unchanged: the full browser suite covering the demo app passes at its original case count on the refactored tree, with no spec file, case or project removed, skipped or pragmatically guarded.
rubrics.rationale: The repository's Playwright suite (98 executable cases across its two browser projects) pins the DOM and store behavior - data attributes, class names, aria labels, timing, promise flows - that the prompt's preservation boundary demands, making suite integrity the instance-specific and non-negotiable regression evidence.

rubrics.criterion: Update-in-place semantics survive the consolidation: rebuilding an already-existing toast - via a promise resolution, a repeated toast() call with a reused id, or a StrictMode-replayed effect - keeps whatever presentation options the update does not restate, and an update that sets icon to null keeps the icon removed instead of resurrecting the stored one.
rubrics.rationale: The injected history contains an update-stability fix whose carry-over list (richColors, invert, unstyled, closeButton, classNames, and an identity ternary for icon because null is meaningful) is the subtlest part of the behavior to move; a consolidation that flattens this path would silently regress what subscribers and the toast history see.

rubrics.criterion: A layer or a falsy/nullish subtlety collapsed inside one of the consolidated families: zero durations now win instead of falling through; an unset option became false (or vice versa) and stopped following the toaster; custom JSX or an unstyled configuration no longer drops the built-in styling; a per-type configured icon stopped winning over the built-in asset or beating a toast-provided one; an expiry ref no longer reseeds from its toast's current duration.
rubrics.rationale: Precedence is exactly where observable regressions hide in this library - several suites assert on a zero duration falling back, on the styled/unstyled combination, and on the configured-icons chain - so each named collapse is a concrete documented behavior with spec coverage, not a hypothetical.

rubrics.criterion: The public surface shifted: exported names or signatures of the package (the Toaster component, the toast function with its success/error/info/warning/loading/message/promise/custom/dismiss methods, useSonner, the shared types) were removed or given new required parameters, or the rendered data attributes and CSS class hooks the suite and stylesheet depend on disappeared from the markup the components emit.
rubrics.rationale: This package's consumers depend on its flat public API and on the data attribute hooks (data-sonner-toast and its family, [data-sonner-toaster]) used for styling and testing; any of those drifting doubles as an unnoticed breaking release, which the task forbids.
